title: Does the pinned Pi version offer a supported route to grant project trust?
statement: Kiln must obtain a project trust decision, because a non-interactive child launched against an untrusted project loads no package and therefore none of Kiln's typed tools, silently. The mechanism is now open. Decision #67(a) chose writing Pi's user trust file directly and proved that causal; the PM withdrew that on 2026-09-02 in favour of a supported public API or native flow. So: does @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.4 expose a documented API, command, or non-interactive option through which a caller can record, read, and revoke a project trust decision?
notes: ⚠️ ITS ANSWER CHANGES A PUBLISHED COMMAND CONTRACT, which is what makes it blocking rather than interesting. If no supported route exists, interactive setup uses Pi's native trust flow, non-interactive setup must require a pre-existing decision or refuse, and the proposed `--trust approve` option is removed or deferred. ⚠️ THE FALLBACK IS EXPLICITLY CLOSED BY PM DIRECTION: a negative answer stops Phase 1 for review and does not authorise reverting to writing the trust file. ⚠️ THE MEASUREMENT NEEDS THE 2026-08-18 CONTROLS — grant, revoke, and explicit denial each observed through a marker written at extension load time, upstream of anything the model says. ⚠️ THE EXPORT LIST WAS CORRECTED 2026-09-11. The answer first named four trust exports; two of them are internal to the package. The load-bearing half is unaffected: `ProjectTrustStore` is a root export and AST-0041's claim about it stands unchanged.
answer: YES. `ProjectTrustStore` is exported from the package root of pi 0.84.4 with a typed declaration — constructor(agentDir), get(cwd), getEntry(cwd), set(cwd, decision), setMany(updates) — alongside `hasTrustRequiringProjectResources`. Those two are the package root's only trust exports: `getProjectTrustOptions` and `getProjectTrustParentPath` are declared in `dist/core/trust-manager.d.ts` but are NOT re-exported from the root, so reaching them would mean importing an unexported path - the boundary DEC-0027 exists to respect. Checked against both the type declarations and the runtime exports of the installed 0.84.4. Measured causal on Windows and Linux with the full control set: a grant loads the package without --approve, an explicit denial prevents loading, and revocation reverts. DEC-0027 is satisfiable exactly as written and the `--trust approve` option can ship. Kiln depends on the exported class; it never writes the trust.json shape.
